Second, you would also have to expect that Mr. Morina independently took it upon himself to travel to the third country, even going so far as to ensure that a hotel room was reserved for Minister Haraqija; and then meet with Witness 2 on two occasions and explain falsely, according to the Haraqija Defence, and in great detail to Witness 2, how he had come to see Witness 2, pursuant to the instructions of Mr. Haraqija. Then you would have to accept that Mr. Morina took it upon himself to discuss with Witness 2 the possibility that Witness 2 would change or withdraw his testimony before this Tribunal in order to protect Ramush Haradinaj. Your Honours, these propositions are simply not reasonable or believable. I'd like to turn for a few moments to the question of Mr. Haraqija's motive. You've heard some evidence about the fact that Mr. Haraqija was the deputy chairman of the committee to defend Ramush Haradinaj. If you take a look, Your Honours, at Exhibit P20, which is an OTP interview with Mr. Haraqija on the 27th of October, 2007, page 12, line 2, to page 13, line 8, in the English; page 12, line 4, to page 13, line 6 in the Albanian, you see that when an investigator asked Mr. Haraqija why he participated in the committee for defence -- for the defence of Ramush Haradinaj, in addition to issues of political parties and balance, Mr. Haraqija explained, "I took part because Rugova authorised me and it's not good to equate the executioner with the victim." By that last phrase, subsequently, Mr. Haraqija explained in the same passage that this Tribunal was equating Slobodan Milosevic and his state apparatus "according to Mr. Haraqija a butcher among the lambs" with the Kosovar Albanians who fought against Serb forces. Mr. Haraqija did not mention this in his testimony today. Page 20 of the same interview, Your Honour, page 14 in the English version and page 14 in the Albanian version, Mr. Haraqija said this: "I don't think of Ramush Haradinaj as an enemy. I think that he fought a just war, and regardless of political convictions, I think he is worthy of support as commander of the KLA as he was." So the evidence from Mr. Haraqija's own words demonstrates that he had a motive to convince -- to instruct Mr. Morina to convince or to discuss with Witness 2 the changing of his testimony against Ramush Haradinaj. In addition, Your Honour, there is evidence that corroborates Mr. Morina's statements that Mr. Haraqija directed Mr. Morina to meet with Witness 2. If you take a look at Exhibit P19, the Prosecution's interview with Mr. Morina from the 26th of October, 2007, page 24, line 29, to page 25, line 13 in the English; page 21, line 36, to page 22, line 5 in the Albanian, Mr. Morina admits that he lied when he told Witness 2 that he had spoken with Astrit Haraqija after their first meeting. According to Mr. Morina: "In other words, I really didn't lie all that much ..." Mr. Morina explained that actually he did not speak with Mr. Haraqija after the first meeting, but that he spoke with the minister's spokesperson, Mr. Veli Bytyqi. Your Honours, that is not the behaviour of a man who is trying to falsely implicate another man in a crime. If Mr. Morina was trying falsely to place the blame for the interference with Witness 2 to Mr. Haraqija, he would have had no rational reason at that moment to distance Mr. Haraqija from this particular point of events. In addition, Your Honour, I would refer you to 65 ter 1A, Exhibit P12, in the English version page 24, lines 1 to 9; in the Albanian version, page 24, lines 25 to 32, where Mr. Morina explains that he was told by Mr. Haraqija to go meet with Witness 2 or "... otherwise it won't be good for you." Then Exhibit P13, recording of the second meeting from the 11th of July, on page 38 of the English version, page 37 of the Albanian version, Witness 2 tells Mr. Morina that he would have liked to speak with Mr. Haraqija. Mr. Morina explains to Witness 2 that he had told

utterances.speaker: MR. HARAQIJA
utterances.text: "I am obliged, I work for you, and I am Albanian and I cannot say no," and that Mr. Morina would arrange and could arrange a meeting between Witness 2 and Mr. Haraqija. I direct your attention to Exhibit P19, the OTP's interview with Mr. Morina from the 26th of October, 2007, page 29 in the English version; page 25 in the Albanian version, where Mr. Morina explains: "I was not in a position to refuse instructions of the minister, and that's why Witness 2 reserved two hotel rooms because until the last minute, the plan was for the minister to go to the third country." And at page 21, line 31, to page 22, line 3, of the English version of the same exhibit; page 19 in the Albanian version, Mr. Morina explained that Mr. Haraqija told Mr. Morina that Witness 2 was one of three persons who could save Ramush Haradinaj. I direct your attention to Exhibit P22, the very first page, which contains the request for travel authorisation that includes both names; the first page in the English version. I would also direct your attention to Exhibit P18, which was an intercepted conversation between -- an intercepted telephone conversation purportedly between Ms. Krasniqi and Mr. Morina. And at page 4 of the English version, you will see that Ms. Krasniqi says to Mr. Morina: "It's unacceptable to put all the guilt on you and not on the minister." And you also hear Ms. Krasniqi referring to "the big one" who sent him. And in the Prosecution's submission, Your Honour, there would have been no one bigger or with more authority in the Ministry of Culture than Minister Haraqija. And that last exhibit dovetails, Your Honours, with Exhibit P10, the Prosecution's interview with Ms. Krasniqi on the 27th of May, 2008, page 9, line 17, to page 10, line 15 in the English version; pages 12 to 13 in the Albanian version, where in discussing that intercept, Exhibit P18, Ms. Krasniqi acknowledged that in this intercept, she was expressing sympathy to Mr. Morina because after Minister Haraqija had sent Mr. Morina to the third country, all of the responsibility for these events was being placed on Mr. Morina. And in the same portion of that interview with Ms. Krasniqi, she also acknowledges that in this telephone conversation with Mr. Morina, she is expressing frustration and annoyance that Minister Haraqija was not taking responsibility for actions that he instigated and was not placing the blame -- and was placing the blame solely on an employee. Today Mr. Haraqija acknowledged, Your Honours, that he could direct ministry employees to travel to certain events abroad. So, clearly, Mr. Haraqija had the executive power to approve such travel, and he executed that power. If you take a look at Exhibit Number 4, the SMS text messages for Mr. Morina to Witness 2, where they refer -- the last five or six messages refer to Mr. Morina and Mr. Haraqija and a need to reserve a hotel room for the minister. I would submit, Your Honour, that there would have been no need for Mr. Morina to have written such a message had there not have been an intention for the minister to go as well. In addition, Mr. Haraqija's agenda, his work agenda, was completely free for the 11th of July, 2007, Exhibit 32, the day he would have met with Witness 2. Your Honours, the totality of Mr. Haraqija's actions in this matter amounted to contempt of the Tribunal as well as incitement to contempt, and I say that because Mr. Haraqija took material concrete steps to ensure that the interference occurred. First, Mr. Haraqija provided ideas to Mr. Morina on ways to convince Witness 2 to meet with Mr. Haraqija and Mr. Morina, for example, by telling Mr. Morina to invoke the name of the late President Rugova in his telephone communications with the witness. Secondly -- I'm going to move on, Your Honour, at this time. Your Honour, the indictment alleges that this interference occurred between July and August of 2007. The written statements of Witness 2, which I believe are now Exhibits P7 and P8, demonstrate that the memories of the events of July 2007 remained with the witness through August and September of 2007. Indeed, Witness 2's testimony before this Chamber indicates that those memories remain with him until the present day. Therefore, the Prosecution has proven beyond a reasonable doubt that, at a minimum, this interference occurred during July and August 2007, as charged in the indictment. If I may backtrack for one moment, Your Honour. It's the Prosecution's understanding that the Defence of Mr. Morina is suggesting that Mr. Morina travelled to the third country to meet with the -- to meet with Witness 2 in order to discuss an article from Bota Sot. If that was the case, Your Honour, then there was no need for Mr. Morina to invoke the name of the late-President Rugova who, as Ms. Krasniqi told us yesterday, continues to be revered by Kosovar Albanians, to convince Witness 2 of the need to meet. Witness 2 mentioned in his statement and on Monday that he was and still is a strong supporter of President Rugova. Mr. Morina could have said simply, It's about an article that I wrote, or it's about an article that I wrote about you. If the purpose of the meeting was simply to discuss an article in Bota Sot, then Mr. Morina had no need to invoke the name and position of the Minister of Culture, Mr. Haraqija, in his telephone conversations leading up to the meetings in July. And while the 2002 article was mentioned in passing during the discussions in the third country between Mr. Morina and Witness 2, it was not the focus of the meetings. The focus of the meetings was the question of whether Witness 2 would change or withdraw his testimony at this Tribunal. And that reference to Bota Sot, to the article, for example, Your Honour, would be in 65 ter -- excuse me, Exhibit P12, the recording of the first meeting, page 16 in the English transcript, page 17 in the Albanian transcript. Another material step that Mr. Haraqija took to ensure that the interference occurred is that we know from Mr. Morina that he -- that Mr. Haraqija approved his travel to the third country. We also can see that, Your Honours -- I'm going to move on. In the moments that I have left, Your Honours, I would like to speak briefly about sentencing. Your Honours, the difficulty faced by the Prosecution in presenting witness testimony in the trial of Mr. Haradinaj are notorious. They were also documented in the Trial Chamber's judgement in that case. And, indeed, at paragraph 6 of the Haradinaj judgement, the Trial Chamber indicated that it had gained a strong impression that the trial was being held in an atmosphere where witnesses felt unsafe. Your Honours, in that context, the conduct of Mr. Morina and Mr. Haraqija was particularly egregious. Furthermore, with respect to Mr. Morina, he abused his authority as a government minister when he committed these crimes. For those reasons, Your Honour, the Prosecution asks, upon a conviction of the two accused for the crimes alleged in the indictment, that you sentence Mr. Morina to a term of imprisonment of one year, and you sentence Mr. Haraqija to a term of imprisonment of two years. Your Honour, that concludes my closing argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Thank you also for staying within the time-limits even more than asked for. The Chamber's considered how to proceed. Tomorrow, we intend to start at 11.30 in the morning. There is, however, a slight chance that not the whole Bench is yet available at that time, in which case the start tomorrow might be delayed until 12.00. It's beyond our control at this moment. Then an opportunity will be given to both Defence counsel to present their closing argument within a similar time-frame, and then there is a little bit of time left for questions by the Bench perhaps on certain matters if they are not clear to us and also to briefly respond to the closing arguments of the other party. We would then conclude certainly not later than a quarter to 2.00. Mr. Registrar, could you tell us in what courtroom we are tomorrow. We'll resume at 11.30 in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of September, 2008, at 11.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.58 p.m.,
